description: Climate Mapping for Resilience and Adaptation (CMRA) is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA Climate Program Office | Communications, Education, & Engagement Division; DOI, U.S. Department of the Interior; USGCRP, U.S. Global Change Research Program. Knowing what hazards your assets might face is the first step in protecting them. This site can help you understand some of the climate-related hazards that could occur in your location, now and in the future. The site's Assessment tool provides climate projections relevant to the five hazards for three future periods. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Air Quality, Drought, Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Extreme Heat, Flooding – Coastal, Flooding – Rainfall-induced, Severe Winter Weather, Wildfire. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Forestry, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Property, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
